ex.crossesAxis: Part of the outline lies on the other side of the axis and will be left out. Draw the outline on one side of the axis.
ex.noLoop: The sketch has no closed outline, so there is nothing to extrude. Close the lines: the end of the last line must meet the start of the first.
ex.problems: Some lines are not closed or cross without a shared point. They are shown in red and will not be part of the shape.
ex.revolveHint: The outline turns around the axis like a part on a lathe: 360° gives a whole solid (a vase, a wheel, a skittle), less gives a part of it.

robo.lampNote: The lamp's program is below: switch it, change its brightness and colour.

blk.distanceTip: Ultrasonic sensor on this port: distance to the nearest thing in front, 2…400 cm (400 = nothing there)
blk.touchTip: Yes when the button of the touch sensor on this port presses against something
blk.lightTip: Light at the light sensor on this port: 0 = dark, 100 = very bright
blk.flashlightTip: Switch the flashlight on this port on or off

blk.whenClickedTip: The blocks below run when this object is clicked during a run
blk.nerpaWalkTip: Walk forward (minus — back); the block waits until the character gets there
blk.nerpaTurnTip: Turn on the spot by this many degrees
blk.nerpaHeadingTip: 0° is along the field's X axis, 90° along Y, −90° the other way
blk.nerpaFaceTip: Turn toward the nearest object of this kind
blk.nerpaGotoTip: Be at this point of the field at once (centimetres)
blk.nerpaGlide: swim to x: %1 y: %2 in %3 s
blk.nerpaGlideTip: Swim smoothly to the point in this many seconds
blk.nerpaJumpTip: Jump; the block waits until the seal lands
blk.nerpaSayTip: A speech bubble over the character; empty text removes it
blk.nerpaSayForTip: Show the bubble, wait, then remove it
blk.nerpaHideTip: Hide the character: invisible, bumps into nothing
blk.nerpaTouchingTip: Yes if the character touches a thing of that kind
blk.nerpaDistanceTip: To the centre of the nearest object of this kind; 10000 (very far) when there is none
blk.nerpaXTip: Where the character is along the field's X axis
blk.nerpaYTip: Where the character is along the field's Y axis
blk.nerpaDirTip: Where the character faces: −180…180°, 0° — along X
blk.lightColorTip: The colour of the light (the light sensor does not tell colours apart)
blk.servoTip: Turn the servo’s shaft to this angle, 0…180°
blk.serialPrintlnTip: Write text or a number to the serial monitor — to see what the program is doing
blk.analogReadTip: The voltage on an analog input: 0 (0 V) … 1023 (5 V)
blk.digitalReadTip: Yes when the pin is HIGH (5 V), no when it is LOW
blk.pinModeTip: How a pin works: input, input with a pull-up to 5 V (a button to GND reads LOW when pressed) or output
blk.toneTip: A sound signal on the pin (for a passive buzzer); it goes on until switched off
blk.toneFor: tone: pin %1 frequency %2 Hz for %3 ms
blk.toneForTip: A sound signal of a given length; the program does not wait for it to end
blk.noToneTip: Stop the sound signal on the pin
blk.lcdPrintTip: Write text on the LCD 1602 connected to SDA (A4) and SCL (A5); columns 0…15
blk.ultrasonicTip: Distance to an obstacle from the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor (2…400 cm; 0 — no echo)
ckt.breadboardHint: 400 holes. The five holes of a column (a–e and f–j) are joined; the + and − rails along the edges run the whole length. Bring a part close and its legs drop into the holes — no wire needed. Parts on the board move with it.
ckt.demo2: Open example: potentiometer, servo and LED
ckt.demo3: Example: a night light with a photoresistor
ckt.demo4: Example: a parking sensor — ultrasonic, display, buzzer
ckt.demo5: Example: a button runs a motor through a transistor
ckt.potHint: The middle pin (W) is the wiper: its voltage moves from one end pin to the other. Connect the ends to 5V and GND, the middle to A0, and read it with the “analog input” block. During a run, turn the knob with the mouse or the wheel.
ckt.servoHint: Three wires: brown to GND, red to 5V, orange (signal) to an Arduino pin. Set the angle 0…180° with the “servo: pin … angle …” block. Without power and ground the servo does not move.
ckt.servoNoPower: The servo does not turn: connect its red wire to 5V and the brown one to GND.
ckt.serialEmpty: What the program prints with the “print to serial monitor” block shows up here. Press Start.
ckt.servoTimer: PWM does not work on pin {pin}: the Servo library takes the timer of pins 9 and 10. Use pin 3, 5, 6 or 11 for the LED.
ckt.roomHint: Things lie on the table next to the circuit; drag them with the mouse, during a run too. Click a lamp to switch it. The sensors see the room: light, warmth, obstacles and motion.
ckt.batteryHint: Power without an Arduino. The red lead is plus, the black one minus. Without an Arduino voltages are measured from the battery's minus.
ckt.meterHint: A voltmeter goes across: the black probe (COM) to minus, the red one to the point you measure. An ammeter goes into the circuit, in series. Change the mode while the circuit is stopped.
ckt.buttonHint: A pressed button joins legs 1 to legs 2 (the legs of a pair are always joined). During a run press it with the mouse. Put it between a pin and GND and set the pin to “input with pull-up”: pressed reads LOW.
ckt.switchHint: The middle leg (C) is joined to leg 1 or leg 2. During a run click to flip it.
ckt.buzzerHint: A passive buzzer sounds with the “tone” block, an active one by itself on HIGH. Plus to the pin, minus to GND.
ckt.rgbHint: Three LEDs in one: red, green, blue; the common cathode (−) is the long leg. Each colour needs its own resistor and pin; PWM mixes the colours.
ckt.ldrHint: Its resistance falls as light falls on it: about 1 kΩ in a lit room, tens of kΩ in the dark. Make a divider with a 10 kΩ resistor and read it on A0. Light comes from the room, lamps on the table and LEDs nearby.
ckt.seg7Hint: Seven LED segments a–g and a dot dp with a common cathode (−). Each segment needs its own resistor and pin.
ckt.motorHint: A motor needs more current than an Arduino pin gives (40 mA): switch it with a transistor and power it from a battery. Put a diode across the motor (cathode to plus).
ckt.npnHint: Legs: emitter (E) to GND, base (B) through a 220 Ω–1 kΩ resistor to a pin, collector (C) to the load. The base current is a hundred times smaller than the load's.
ckt.diodeHint: Lets current through only from the anode (A) to the cathode (K, the striped end).
ckt.lcdHint: A 16×2 display with an I2C board: GND to GND, VCC to 5V, SDA to A4, SCL to A5. Write text with the “display: line … write …” block.
ckt.joystickHint: Two axes are two potentiometers: VRx and VRy to analog inputs, +5V and GND to power. SW is pulled to GND when the stick is pressed. During a run push the stick with the mouse; press it by clicking the board beside it.
ckt.tmp36Hint: Output: 0.5 V at 0 °C plus 10 mV per degree. The temperature is the room's (the slider below) and a hot mug's nearby.
ckt.hcsr04Hint: Looks forward (up in the drawing) and finds a box or a hand on the table within a 30° cone. Read the distance with the “distance, cm: Trig … Echo …” block.
ckt.irHint: OUT goes LOW when there is an obstacle in front (up to 15 cm). Read it with the “digital input” block.
ckt.pirHint: OUT goes HIGH for a couple of seconds when a hand moves in front (up to 5 m, a 110° angle).
robo.terrainHint.platform: Platform: a raised block robots and characters can go on. Drag it onto the field; go up onto it by a ramp
robo.terrainHint.ramp: Ramp: a slope up onto a platform or bridge. Drag it onto the field; track tiles can lie on it. R turns it
robo.terrainHint.bridge: Bridge: a deck between two platforms; you can drive underneath. Drag it onto the field
robo.terrainNote.platform: Robots and characters get onto a platform by a ramp and fall if they go off the edge. Track tiles can lie on top.
robo.terrainNote.ramp: Put the high end against a platform or bridge. Nobody can climb a ramp steeper than about 25°.
robo.terrainNote.bridge: Put it between two platforms of the same height. There is room to pass underneath.
sk.dimLineTip: Click to select the dimension (Delete removes it); drag to move it
sk.c.regular: Regular polygon: corners on the circle, sides equal
part.bolt.head: Head
part.bolt.info: Thread pitch {p} mm, wrench {s} mm. Print it head down. Clearance makes the thread thinner so the nut turns on easily: 0.2 mm is usually enough.
part.nut.info: Thread pitch {p} mm, wrench {s} mm, height {h} mm. Fits a bolt of the same size.
part.jar.info: Thread pitch {p} mm. The jar and the lid are two parts with the same sizes; print the lid top down.
insp.sizeByParams: The size comes from the part settings below, so threads and fits stay exact
part.rack.info: Length {l} mm. Meshes with a gear of the same module ({m}): turning becomes moving in a straight line.
part.wheel.info: Prints lying flat. Put a rubber band or an o-ring in the groove so the wheel grips. The flat-side hole fits motor shafts with a flat.
part.pulley.info: A groove for a round belt, a rubber band or an o-ring {s} mm thick. Two pulleys of different sizes make a drive: the smaller one turns faster.
part.pulley.infoV: A groove for a {s} mm V-belt. Two pulleys of different sizes make a drive: the smaller one turns faster.
part.spring.info: Height {h} mm. A thicker wire makes it stiffer, a bigger pitch softer with a longer travel. A plastic spring is weaker than a steel one: try it out.
part.boxLid.info: The box and the lid are two parts with the same sizes. The lid prints rim up and fits on top.
part.boxLid.infoSlide: The box and the lid are two parts with the same sizes. The lid slides in from the front along grooves in the walls.
part.hinge.info: Prints already assembled and turns straight away: the pin is inside. If it comes out stuck, raise the clearance to 0.5 mm.
part.knob.info: Underneath is a pocket for an {s} nut: press it in and screw in a bolt to get a knob turned by hand.
part.tag.info: The tag grows with the text. The letters can be printed in another colour: change the filament at the right height.
sk.freeHint: What is already pinned down has the finished colour; the rest can still move.
robo.landHint: Drag onto the field — it takes a whole cell (replacing what was there). Or turn the brush on and paint
robo.brushHint: Brush: drag over the field to cover cells (Shift — rectangle, Ctrl — line)
robo.eraserHint: Eraser: drag over the field to remove landscape cells (Shift — rectangle, Ctrl — line)
robo.brushNote: Drag over the field with the left button held. With Shift — fill a rectangle, with Ctrl — a straight line. Esc turns the brush off
robo.eraserNote: Drag over the cells to remove. With Shift — a rectangle, with Ctrl — a straight line. Esc turns the eraser off
robo.terrainNote.ground: A low cell of ground: every robot and character can go onto it. The line sensor sees the surface (grass is darker than sand), and the black line on a road.
robo.terrainNote.water: The robot and the cheetah stop at the shore; the seal swims. A bridge between platforms can cross the water.
robo.decorHint: Drag onto the field. Trees, bushes and rocks are obstacles: robots and characters stop at them and the sonar sees them. Flowers can be driven over
robo.cheetahHint: Cheetie the cheetah: walks, runs fast and jumps onto ledges. Cannot swim — stops at the water. His program is below
robo.pigeonHint: Gennady the pigeon: walks slowly, takes off, flies over anything and lands on dry ground — never on water. His program is below
robo.cheetahNote: Cheetie stops at a ledge and at the water. “jump forward” takes him one cell ahead — onto a platform up to 17 cm high, a rock, or down. “crawl” gets him under a low bridge.
robo.pigeonNote: In the air Gennady passes over everything lower than him and bumps into anything taller. He will not land on water — he says so.
blk.cheetahRunTip: Run forward — three times faster than walking; the block waits until he gets there
blk.cheetahLeapTip: A jump one cell ahead: onto a ledge up to 17 cm high, onto a rock, or down. Too high or into water — he jumps on the spot
blk.pigeonTakeoffTip: Rise to this height above the ground (in the air — change height)
blk.pigeonFlyTip: Fly forward at his height; from the ground he first takes off to 40 cm
blk.pigeonFlyToTip: Turn to a point of the field and fly to it (centimetres)
blk.pigeonLandTip: Come down onto whatever is below. Never on water — he says so
blk.creatureLedgeTip: Yes if right ahead there is something higher than a step: a platform's side, a ramp's side
blk.creatureWaterTip: Yes if there is water right ahead (in flight — water below ahead)
blk.nerpaInWaterTip: Yes if the seal is swimming now
blk.pigeonAltitudeTip: How high above the ground (0 — on the ground)

mods.title: Mods
mods.none: No mods. A mod is a folder with a mod.json file and 3D models (your own robot, for example). Put it into the mods folder and restart the app; mod.json is described in MODS.md in the source code.
mods.hint: A new mod: put its folder into the mods folder and restart the app.
mods.missing: The project has things from mods that are not installed here ({ids}): robots are shown as NerpaBot, heroes as the usual ones, pieces as plain shapes. The file keeps them as they are.
mods.pieceBroken: Could not load the model of the piece “{id}” from its mod
robo.modPieceHint: A piece from a mod: drag it onto the field or click.
robo.modHeroHint: A hero from a mod: moves like {like}. Drag it onto the field or click.
robo.islandTip: An island in the sea: the robot drives along the road, the seal swims round, Cheetie jumps over the hill, Gennady flies, the lighthouse blinks
help.brushDo: paint landscape cells (the eraser rubs them out)
help.brushCtrl: a straight line of cells (a road)
help.brushEsc: brush: undo the stroke or put the brush away
help.terrainDo: landscape, relief and scenery: drag a button onto a cell; R turns platforms and ramps. Relief is built in tiers: a platform or ramp stands on what is under it (grass, another platform) and follows it
help.heroesDo: the seal swims; Cheetie runs, jumps onto ledges up to 17 cm and crawls under a bridge (if the gap is at least 2/3 of his height); Gennady takes off and flies. Each has only its own blocks
help.soundsDo: the characters' “Sound” section: their own voices, common sounds and notes; heard only during a run, the overall volume is the slider under “Speed”
help.prettyDo: in the “Run” section: day, evening or night, the sun, glow, shadows; on a slow computer the quality goes down by itself
help.lineSensorDo: sees surfaces by brightness: water 20, grass 62, stone 68, sand 86, road 90, black line 0
help.examplesDo: “Open the demo” and “Island demo” — at the bottom of the right panel
blk.msgWhenTip: Runs the blocks below when someone on the field broadcasts this message. If they are still running, they start over
blk.msgSendTip: Send the message to everyone on the field (robot, characters, lamps) and go on at once
blk.msgSendWaitTip: Send the message and wait until everyone who got it has finished
help.messagesDo: “broadcast” starts “when I receive” for everyone on the field — robots, characters and lamps; “…and wait” waits until they finish; a new name is “New message…” in the list
blk.creatureUnderTip: What I stand on: grass, sand, stone, road, water, floor, platform, ramp, bridge, track tile, rock; in flight — air
blk.creatureOnTip: Yes if I stand on this (in flight only “air”)
blk.creatureAheadIsTip: Yes if this is right in front of me (where I'd step; in flight — what is below ahead)
help.surfaceDo: the characters' “Sensors”: “under me” (a word), “standing on …?”, “… ahead?” — grass, sand, stone, road, water, floor, platform, ramp, bridge, track tile, rock, air. The robot finds out only with its sensors
blk.cheetahCrawlTip: Crouch and crawl forward (slower than walking). This gets under a bridge if the gap is at least 2/3 of my height; I stand up again when there is room above me
robo.followTip: During a run the camera keeps the selected robot or character in view (you can still turn and zoom). Or double-click it during a run
robo.shotTip: Save a picture of the view as it is now (PNG); in the beautiful view, the beautiful one
robo.videoTip: Record up to 10 seconds of the view (WebM); press again to stop earlier
help.cameraDo: in the “Run” section: “Follow” keeps the selected robot or character in view (or double-click it during a run); “Picture” saves a PNG; “Video” records up to 10 s (WebM)
recover.title: Restore the project?
recover.text: Last time the app closed without saving the project “{name}”. There is an autosave of it from {when}. Restore it?
start.title: Recent projects
start.none: Nothing yet: projects you save and open will show up here.
start.missing: The project file was not found: it may have been moved or deleted. It was taken off the list.
start.forget: Take off the list (the file itself stays)
